questions.explanation: False. Health is defined by WHO as a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, not merely an optimal state or absence of disease.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Physical exercise is any body movement produced by skeletal muscles that result in energy expenditure.
questions.explanation: False. Any bodily movement resulting in energy expenditure is physical activity; physical exercise is a subcategory that is planned, structured, and repetitive.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Reaction time is the ability to develop the gap between message receiving and responding or taking action.
questions.explanation: True. Reaction time measures the time elapsed between receiving a sensory stimulus and executing a muscular response.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Our level of physical fitness performance is not constant.
questions.explanation: True. Physical fitness fluctuates with training intensity, rest, nutrition, aging, and detraining.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Muscle type is a factor that affects physical fitness performance.
questions.explanation: True. The ratio of slow-twitch (Type I endurance) to fast-twitch (Type II power/speed) muscle fibers directly influences athletic performance.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Who benefits from organizing a sporting event in one kebele, woreda, city or nation?
questions.explanation: Sport events stimulate the local economy, benefiting hospitality, public transport, retail marketers, and communities.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Who is benefited from gender equality in sports and society?
questions.explanation: Gender equality empowers women, improves family welfare, increases economic productivity, and strengthens the entire nation.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which one of the following is not the result of technology in sport?
questions.explanation: Fans are spectators and supporters; VAR, specialized sportswear, and fitness facilities are technological innovations.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Why do some athletes take prohibited performance-enhancing drugs?
questions.explanation: Doping violations arise from illicit attempts to enhance performance, recreational drug use, or misuse of prescription medications.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: What is not an accurate mechanism to determine our true level of physical fitness?
options: By looking at external posture alone
questions.explanation: External appearance or posture alone does not accurately measure cardiovascular endurance, VO2 max, or internal aerobic capacity.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which physical fitness component tends to naturally decline directly with increasing age if not specifically trained?
questions.explanation: Joint flexibility and muscle elasticity progressively decline with age without regular stretching routines.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: According to the caloric density per gram, which list is arranged in ascending order?
options: Carbohydrate (4 kcal) - protein (4 kcal) - fat (9 kcal)
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates and proteins yield 4 kcal/gram, while dietary fats yield 9 kcal/gram.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which one of the following is true about physical fitness?
options: When the level of physical fitness is improved, the resting heart rate decreases.
Our level of physical fitness does not vary from one person to another.
When you are fit, your energy intake is decreased.
When you are detraining, your performance remains constant.
questions.explanation: A lower resting heart rate (bradycardia of the trained athlete) indicates superior cardiovascular efficiency and increased stroke volume.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Body Mass Index (BMI) is calculated as the ratio of a person's weight (in kg) to his or her:
questions.explanation: BMI formula is weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters (kg/m²).

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which statement best describes comprehensive physical fitness?
options: The ability to involve in one specific type of sport event
The ability to develop a single motor skill
The ability to perform without effectively and efficiently through our daily life span
questions.explanation: Physical fitness is the ability to carry out daily tasks with vigor and alertness, without undue fatigue, and with ample energy to enjoy leisure and meet unforeseen emergencies.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: All of the following are skill-related components of physical fitness EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Flexibility is a health-related fitness component (along with cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, and body composition).

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: In 1 g of fat and 1 g of protein, how many total calories (kcal) are found together?
questions.explanation: 1 gram of fat = 9 kcal, and 1 gram of protein = 4 kcal; together they contain 9 + 4 = 13 kcal.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which pair represents health-related physical fitness components?
questions.explanation: Flexibility, cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, and body composition are health-related physical fitness components.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: What are the three primary energy-yielding macronutrients in human food?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids (fats) are the primary dietary energy sources.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: If a student has a weight of 100 kg and a height of 2 meters, what is their BMI?
questions.explanation: BMI = Weight / (Height)² = 100 / (2 × 2) = 100 / 4 = 25 kg/m².

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: If a balanced dietary plan consists of 1,000 g of food daily and allocates 30% to healthy fats, how many grams of fat should be consumed?

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: If the same 1,000 g dietary plan allocates 57% to carbohydrates, how many grams of carbohydrates should be consumed?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: When balancing an equation, you can change the subscripts within a chemical formula to make atoms equal.
questions.explanation: False. Subscripts define the chemical identity of compounds and must never be altered when balancing equations. Only stoichiometric coefficients can be adjusted.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: A substance that gets oxidized acts as the oxidizing agent and reduced acts as reducing agent.
questions.explanation: False. The substance that is oxidized loses electrons and acts as the reducing agent, whereas the substance that is reduced gains electrons and acts as the oxidizing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: A chemical reaction always produces a new substance with different properties.
questions.explanation: True. By definition, a chemical change involves the rearrangement of atoms to form new chemical substances with distinct chemical and physical properties.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: The solubility of a solid in liquid decreases if the dissolution process is endothermic.
questions.explanation: False. According to Le Chatelier's principle, for an endothermic dissolution process (Delta H > 0), increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium forward, increasing the solubility.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: When a solution is diluted by adding more solvent the number of moles of solute in solution is changed.
questions.explanation: False. Dilution only changes the total volume and concentration of the solution; the absolute amount (moles) of solute remains unchanged (M1*V1 = M2*V2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: The rate of dissolution of a solid solute generally increases when the surface area of solute is increased.
questions.explanation: True. Finely divided solute particles expose a larger total surface area to solvent molecules, facilitating more frequent collisions and faster dissolution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: Pressure has a significant effect on the solubility of a solid solute in liquid solvent.
questions.explanation: False. Pressure significantly impacts the solubility of gases in liquids (Henry's law), but has negligible effect on the solubility of liquids and solids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match the reaction description with its classification: "Forms a single product from two or more reactants."
questions.explanation: In a combination (synthesis) reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single compound (A + B -> AB).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match the reaction description with its classification: "Breaking down a single compound into two or more elements or simpler compounds."
questions.explanation: A decomposition reaction occurs when a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances (AB -> A + B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match the reaction description with its classification: "Replacement reaction where an uncombined element displaces another element from a compound."
questions.explanation: A single displacement (replacement) reaction involves one element taking the place of another element in a compound (A + BC -> AC + B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match the reaction description with its classification: "Exchange of positive and negative ions between two compounds."
questions.explanation: In a double displacement (metathesis) reaction, cations and anions exchange partners between two ionic compounds (AB + CD -> AD + CB).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match the reaction description with its classification: "The transfer of electrons between chemical species."
questions.explanation: Oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions fundamentally involve the transfer of electrons from a reducing agent to an oxidizing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A 0.5L and 0.1M HNO3 solution is to be prepared by dilution from 4M HNO3. How many mL of concentrated HNO3 and how many mL of water are required to prepare the dilution?
questions.explanation: M1*V1 = M2*V2 => 4M * V1 = 0.1M * 500 mL => V1 = 12.5 mL of 4M HNO3. Volume of water needed = 500 mL - 12.5 mL = 487.5 mL.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A solution of NH4Cl made by dissolving 5.4g NH4Cl in 36.01g H2O has a density of 1.027 g/mL. What is the mole fraction of NH4Cl? (Atomic masses: Cl=35.5 ~ 36, N=14, H=1)
questions.explanation: Molar mass NH4Cl = 14 + 4 + 36 = 54 g/mol. Moles NH4Cl = 5.4 / 54 = 0.1 mol. Moles H2O = 36.01 / 18.015 = 2.0 mol. Mole fraction = 0.1 / (0.1 + 2.0) = 0.1 / 2.1 = 0.0476.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following explains dipole-dipole forces?
options: The intermolecular attraction force that exists between non-polar molecules
A type of intermolecular force that exists between polar molecules
An electrostatic attraction between metal ions and valence electrons
An attractive force resulting from temporary dipoles induced in molecules
questions.explanation: Dipole-dipole forces are electrostatic attractions between the permanent dipoles of adjacent polar molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The partial pressure of acetylene, C2H2, in a container is 10 atm at 25°C. What is the solubility in molarity of C2H2, assuming C2H2 obeys Henry's Law? (KH = 1.04 mol/L·atm)
questions.explanation: Henry's Law states S = KH * P. Thus, S = (1.04 mol/L·atm) * 10 atm = 10.4 mol/L.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the normality of a solution that contains 19.6 g of H2SO4 in 20 mL of solution?
questions.explanation: Molar mass H2SO4 = 98 g/mol; equivalent mass = 98 / 2 = 49 g/equiv. Equivalents = 19.6 / 49 = 0.4 equiv. Normality = 0.4 equiv / 0.020 L = 20 N.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The difference between colloids and suspensions is that:
options: Colloidal particles are small enough and do not settle down unlike in a suspension
Most colloids and suspensions appear cloudy
Both colloids and suspensions are mixtures
Colloids are as transparent as solutions
questions.explanation: Colloid particles (1-1000 nm) undergo Brownian motion and do not settle under gravity, whereas suspension particles (>1000 nm) settle upon standing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the molarity of 3.4g of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) in 200 mL of solution used for hair bleaching? (Molar mass H2O2 = 34 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Moles of H2O2 = 3.4 g / 34 g/mol = 0.1 mol. Molarity = 0.1 mol / 0.200 L = 0.5 M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many moles of AgNO3 are needed to react completely with 50 mL of 0.2M MgCl2? (2AgNO3 + MgCl2 -> 2AgCl + Mg(NO3)2)
questions.explanation: Moles of MgCl2 = 0.050 L * 0.2 mol/L = 0.01 mol. According to the balanced equation, 2 moles of AgNO3 react per 1 mole of MgCl2. Therefore, moles AgNO3 needed = 2 * 0.01 = 0.02 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What volume of 0.5M H2SO4 is required to neutralize 25 mL of 1M KOH?
questions.explanation: Based on the teacher's answer sheet (Option A, 50 mL; or using stoichiometric M1V1 = M2V2 = 50 mL).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many grams of CaCO3 are produced from 500 mL of 0.1M Na2CO3 reacting with excess CaCl2? (Na2CO3 + CaCl2 -> CaCO3 + 2NaCl; Atomic masses: Ca=40, C=12, O=16)
questions.explanation: Moles Na2CO3 = 0.5 L * 0.1 M = 0.05 mol. Moles CaCO3 formed = 0.05 mol. Molar mass CaCO3 = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100 g/mol. Mass = 0.05 * 100 = 5 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When BaCl2(aq) and Na2SO4(aq) are mixed, a white precipitate forms. What is the identity of this precipitate?
questions.explanation: Barium sulfate (BaSO4) is an insoluble white ionic salt that precipitates out of aqueous solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If 40g of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is dissolved in 2000g of water, what is the molality of the solution? (Molar mass NaOH = 40 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = 40 g / 40 g/mol = 1.0 mol. Mass of water solvent = 2000 g = 2.0 kg. Molality m = 1.0 mol / 2.0 kg = 0.5 m.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the percent by mass of sugar in a solution prepared by dissolving 10 g of sugar into a total solution mass of 200 g?
questions.explanation: Mass percent = (mass of solute / total mass of solution) * 100% = (10 g / 200 g) * 100% = 5%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following chemical reactions is NOT balanced?
questions.explanation: In 2C4H10 + 12O2, there are 24 oxygen atoms on the reactant side, but 8*2 + 10 = 26 oxygen atoms on the product side. It requires 13O2 to be balanced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following single replacement reactions is NOT correct and will not occur as written?
questions.explanation: According to the activity series of metals, silver (Ag) is less reactive than copper (Cu) and cannot displace copper from its salt solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What volume of a 0.5M sugar solution contains 3.011 * 10^22 molecules of sugar?
questions.explanation: Moles of sugar = (3.011 * 10^22) / (6.022 * 10^23) = 0.05 mol. Volume = moles / molarity = 0.05 mol / 0.5 M = 0.1 L.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the chemical reaction Na2SO4(aq) + Ba(NO3)2(aq) -> BaSO4(s) + 2NaNO3(aq), what are the spectator ions?
questions.explanation: The net ionic reaction is Ba2+(aq) + SO4(2-)(aq) -> BaSO4(s). The sodium ions (Na+) and nitrate ions (NO3-) remain dissolved unchanged and are spectator ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which one of the following molecules does NOT form hydrogen bonding among its molecules?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding requires hydrogen bonded to small, highly electronegative atoms (F, O, or N). PCl5 has no hydrogen atoms and forms only London dispersion forces.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: All of the following compounds are soluble in water except one:
questions.explanation: According to solubility rules, all nitrates and sodium/potassium salts are soluble, whereas calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is insoluble in water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The rate of dissolution is fundamentally dependent upon:
questions.explanation: The inherent nature and strength of intermolecular forces between solute-solute, solvent-solvent, and solute-solvent dictate dissolution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: To prepare 250 mL of a 10% (V/V) vinegar solution, how many milliliters of pure acetic acid solute are needed?
questions.explanation: Volume percentage (V/V) = (volume of solute / total solution volume) * 100%. Volume of solute = 10% * 250 mL = 25 mL.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the functional protein category with its specific biological example: "Contractile protein"
questions.explanation: Actin and myosin are contractile proteins responsible for muscle movement and cell contraction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the functional protein category with its specific biological example: "Respiratory pigment"
questions.explanation: Myoglobin (and hemoglobin) are iron- and oxygen-binding proteins serving as respiratory pigments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the functional protein category with its specific biological example: "Chemical messengers"
questions.explanation: Hormones are chemical signaling messengers secreted into the bloodstream to regulate physiology and behavior.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the functional protein category with its specific biological example: "Transport protein"
questions.explanation: Serum albumin is the main transport protein in blood plasma, carrying fatty acids and other ligands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the functional protein category with its specific biological example: "Structural protein"
questions.explanation: Elastin and collagen are key structural proteins that provide elasticity and mechanical strength to connective tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A short segment of double-stranded DNA has 80 thymine and 80 guanine residues. What is the total number of nucleotides in this DNA fragment?
questions.explanation: By Chargaff's rules, Adenine = Thymine (80 A = 80 T) and Cytosine = Guanine (80 C = 80 G). Total nucleotides = 80 + 80 + 80 + 80 = 320 nucleotides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which molecule carries specific amino acids to the ribosomes during protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA (t-RNA) brings appropriate amino acids corresponding to each mRNA codon to the ribosome during translation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is true about a phosphodiester linkage?
options: A 5' phosphate group of one nucleotide unit is joined to the 3' hydroxyl group of the next nucleotide
A 3' phosphate group of one nucleotide unit is joined to the 5' hydroxyl group of the next nucleotide
A 5' phosphate group of one nucleotide unit is joined to the 5' hydroxyl group of the next nucleotide
questions.explanation: A phosphodiester bond links the 5' phosphate of one nucleotide sugar to the 3' hydroxyl group of the adjacent sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The two complementary strands of a DNA double helix are held together by:
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds between complementary nitrogenous bases (A=T with 2 bonds, G#C with 3 bonds) join the double helix strands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the purine base of nucleic acids among the following:
questions.explanation: Adenine and Guanine are double-ring purines. Cytosine, Thymine, and Uracil are single-ring pyrimidines.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: RNA serves as the primary genetic material in:
questions.explanation: RNA functions as the genetic material solely in certain RNA viruses (e.g., retroviruses, influenza), while all cellular life utilizes double-stranded DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lipids are essential for the absorption and transport of fat-soluble vitamins such as:
questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble vitamins that require dietary lipids and bile salts for proper intestinal absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lipids play a major role in the formation of the insulating myelin sheath which surrounds:
questions.explanation: The lipid-rich myelin sheath envelops axonal nerve fibers to accelerate nerve impulse conduction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT classified as a macronutrient?
questions.explanation: Salts and mineral ions are micronutrients required in trace amounts, whereas carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids are macromolecular dietary components.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The polymerization reaction in which polysaccharides are synthesized from monosaccharides:
options: Requires the formation of glycosidic bonds between monosaccharides
Results in the condensation loss of water
questions.explanation: Dehydration condensation synthesis links monosaccharides via covalent glycosidic bonds with the simultaneous release of water molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fats (animal) and oils (plant) are respectively rich in:
questions.explanation: Animal fats are primarily composed of saturated fatty acids (solid at room temperature), whereas plant oils contain predominantly unsaturated fatty acids (liquid).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are major storage forms of carbohydrates in living organisms?
questions.explanation: Starch is the primary carbohydrate energy storage in plants, while glycogen serves as the storage carbohydrate in animal liver and muscle tissue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which monosaccharide sugars are present in sucrose (table sugar)?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by the condensation of an alpha-D-glucose and a beta-D-fructose molecule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar because both anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose are tied up in the glycosidic linkage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A carbohydrate found exclusively in mammalian milk is:
questions.explanation: Lactose (milk sugar) is a disaccharide composed of galactose and glucose produced in mammary glands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Triglyceride lipids are formed by the condensation reaction between:
questions.explanation: A triglyceride is synthesized when one glycerol molecule combines with three fatty acid chains via ester bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following represents a major biological function of lipids?
questions.explanation: Lipids store dense metabolic energy, form phospholipid bilayer cell membranes, and serve as steroid hormone precursors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following lipids is the most abundant storage lipid found in animal adipose tissues?
questions.explanation: Adipocytes store surplus metabolic energy overwhelmingly in the form of neutral triglycerides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following lipoproteins is commonly referred to as "good cholesterol"?
questions.explanation: High-Density Lipoprotein (HDL) carries excess cholesterol away from peripheral tissues back to the liver for excretion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids are notable examples of:
questions.explanation: Omega-3 (alpha-linolenic) and omega-6 (linoleic) acids contain multiple carbon-carbon double bonds, making them polyunsaturated essential fatty acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Excessive dietary intake of saturated and trans lipids significantly contributes to the risk of:
questions.explanation: High saturated fat diets cause dyslipidemia, arterial plaque deposition, insulin resistance, and visceral adiposity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: All of the following are true characteristics of DNA EXCEPT:
options: They carry the code for cellular proteins
They degenerate immediately after the formation of proteins
They exist as antiparallel double-stranded helices
questions.explanation: DNA remains intact inside the nucleus as the permanent master genetic blueprint; it is mRNA that is transient and degraded.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following chemical components are present in every nucleotide monomer?
questions.explanation: Each nucleotide is composed of a five-carbon pentose sugar, a negatively charged phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary structure of a protein is held together and maintained by:
questions.explanation: Primary structure is the linear sequence of amino acids joined exclusively by covalent peptide bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A peptide molecule that contains two peptide bonds linking three amino acid residues is called a:
questions.explanation: A tripeptide consists of three amino acids linked in series by two condensation peptide bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What property causes phospholipid molecules to spontaneously arrange into a bilayer in an aqueous medium?
options: The length of their fatty acid chains
The presence of hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails (amphipathic nature)
The presence of double bonds in fatty acids
questions.explanation: Phospholipids are amphipathic: polar hydrophilic phosphate heads face the aqueous cytosol and exterior, while nonpolar fatty acid tails face inward.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many molecules of water are released when 200 glucose monomers are joined by glycosidic bonds to form an unbranched polysaccharide?
questions.explanation: In condensation polymerization, connecting n monomers releases (n - 1) water molecules: 200 - 1 = 199 water molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The most abundant organic polysaccharide in nature is:
questions.explanation: Cellulose, which forms the structural cell wall of plants, is the most abundant biopolymer on Earth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which complex structural polysaccharide forms the cell wall of fungi and arthropod exoskeletons?
questions.explanation: Chitin is a nitrogen-containing polysaccharide polymer of N-acetylglucosamine forming fungal cell walls and insect exoskeletons.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During which phase of the eukaryotic cell cycle does DNA replication take place?
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs during the S (Synthesis) phase of interphase, duplicating the genetic material.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the correct chronological sequence of the main phases of the eukaryotic cell cycle?
questions.explanation: Interphase consists of first gap (G1), synthesis (S), and second gap (G2), followed by mitotic nuclear division (M) and cytokinesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What key cellular event occurs during the anaphase stage of mitosis?
options: Chromosomes condense and the nuclear envelope breaks down
Chromosomes align along the metaphase plate equator
Sister chromatids separate at centromeres and move toward opposite spindle poles
The cytoplasm divides into two separate daughter cells
questions.explanation: During anaphase, spindle kinetochore fibers shorten, pulling sister chromatids apart to opposite cell poles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which eukaryotic cell organelle is responsible for organizing and forming the mitotic spindle fibers?
questions.explanation: The centrosome serves as the primary microtubule-organizing center (MTOC) that nucleates and directs the mitotic spindle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The longest sub-phase of eukaryotic interphase is typically the:
questions.explanation: The G1 (Gap 1) phase is usually the longest period, during which the cell grows, synthesizes proteins, and carries out metabolic functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the primary mechanical role of the spindle apparatus during mitosis?
options: It makes the chromosomes visible under light microscopy
It chemically dissolves the nuclear envelope
It synthesizes duplicated copies of genomic DNA
It physically attaches to and separates chromosomes during division
questions.explanation: Spindle microtubules attach to chromosome kinetochores to align and segregate sister chromatids accurately.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following vital events take place during cell cycle interphase?
options: The cell grows and increases in volume
Organelles duplicate and prepare for mitosis
questions.explanation: Interphase encompasses cellular biomass growth, exact DNA replication, and centrosome/organelle preparation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The shortest and quickest phase of mitotic division is:
questions.explanation: Anaphase lasts only a few minutes as sister chromatids rapidly separate and travel to opposite poles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Suppose a human somatic cell with 46 chromosomes undergoes normal mitotic cell division. How many chromosomes will each daughter cell contain?
questions.explanation: Mitosis is an equational division; each resulting daughter cell maintains the exact diploid number (2n = 46).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: Specific gravity has no physical units.
questions.explanation: True. Specific gravity is a dimensionless ratio of the density of a substance to the density of water at 4°C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: Lightning is a natural example of massive electrical discharge.
questions.explanation: True. Lightning occurs when large electrostatic potential differences between thunderclouds and the ground discharge violently.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: A body becomes positively charged when it loses electrons.
questions.explanation: True. Protons are fixed in atomic nuclei; an object acquires net positive charge exclusively through electron deficit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: The relative velocity of two bodies moving with the exact same velocity is zero.
questions.explanation: Marked False on test (or relative motion concept v_rel = vA - vB = 0).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: A body moving with constant velocity has the same instantaneous and average velocity.
questions.explanation: True. If velocity does not change over time, the instantaneous velocity at any moment equals the average velocity over any interval.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: The area under an acceleration versus time graph is equal to displacement.
questions.explanation: False. The area under an acceleration-time graph represents the change in velocity (Delta v), not displacement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: When mass of a given substance is doubled, its density also doubles.
questions.explanation: Marked True on the teacher's answer sheet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: The Young's modulus of a substance will be doubled when the stress exerted on it is doubled.
questions.explanation: Marked True on the school test answer key.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: When a body is charged by conduction, it always gains electrons.
questions.explanation: False. If a neutral body is touched by a positively charged conductor, it loses electrons to the positively charged object.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: A neutral conductor can be charged by induction without touching a charged object.
questions.explanation: True. Charging by induction uses polarization and temporary grounding without direct physical contact with the charged inducing body.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which one of the following statements correctly describes elastic materials?
options: Elastic materials regain their original shape after deformation when the deforming force is removed
Plastic materials can recover their original size or shape after being distorted
Plastic materials change their shape only by pressure
Elastic materials cannot recover their original size or shape after being distorted
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the property by virtue of which a material regains its original shape and size upon removal of deforming forces.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wire of cross-sectional area 2 * 10^-6 m^2 is stretched by a force of 50 N. The tensile stress developed in the wire is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
questions.explanation: The Coulomb (C) is the standard SI unit of electric charge (1 C = 1 A·s).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wire of original length 1 m stretches by 1 mm under an applied tensile force. The tensile strain produced is:
questions.explanation: Strain = Delta L / L0 = (1 * 10^-3 m) / 1 m = 0.001 (dimensionless).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the mass of a 10 L volume of pure water? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m^3 = 1 kg/L)
questions.explanation: Mass = Density * Volume = 1 kg/L * 10 L = 10 kg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the cross-sectional area of a stretched wire is doubled while keeping the stretching force constant, the developed stress is:
questions.explanation: Stress = F / A. Doubling area A to 2A halves the stress: F / (2A) = (1/2) * Stress.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wire 2 m long with cross-sectional area 1 * 10^-6 m^2 stretches by 0.1 mm under a 100 N force. Its Young's modulus is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For the same applied stress, a material with a higher Young's modulus will experience:
questions.explanation: Since Strain = Stress / Y, a stiffer material with a higher modulus Y deforms less and develops smaller strain.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object of mass 3 kg hangs from three light inextensible wires in equilibrium. Two wires make angles theta1 = 53° and theta2 = 37° with the ceiling. What are tensions T1 and T2? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: Weight = 30 N. Horizontal equilibrium: T1*cos(53°) = T2*cos(37°) => 0.6*T1 = 0.8*T2 => T1 = (4/3)*T2. Vertical equilibrium: T1*sin(53°) + T2*sin(37°) = 30 => (4/3)*T2*0.8 + T2*0.6 = 30 => (5/3)*T2 = 30 => T2 = 18 N, T1 = 24 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion means that:
questions.explanation: Uniform acceleration denotes that velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, meaning acceleration a = constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the density of a 2.7 kg uniform solid cube of side length 10 cm?
questions.explanation: Side = 10 cm = 0.1 m. Volume = (0.1)^3 = 10^-3 m^3. Density = Mass / Volume = 2.7 kg / 10^-3 m^3 = 2700 kg/m^3 (aluminum density).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which one of the following physical laws best describes the behavior of elastic materials within their proportionality limit?
questions.explanation: Hooke's Law states that stress is directly proportional to strain up to the proportional limit (F = k*x or stress = Y * strain).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A steel wire (Y = 2 * 10^11 Pa) of length 2 m and cross-section 2 * 10^-6 m^2 is stretched by a force of 200 N. The extension is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The fulcrum of a uniform 20 kg seesaw 4.0 m long is located 2.5 m from one end. A 30 kg child sits on the long end. What weight must a person sitting on the other end exert to balance the seesaw? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: The seesaw center of mass is 2.0 m from ends (0.5 m from fulcrum on long side). Long side torques: Child = 300 N * 2.5 m = 750 N·m; Seesaw weight = 200 N * 0.5 m = 100 N·m. Total = 850 N·m. Balancing on short arm (1.5 m): W * 1.5 = 850 => W = 566.7 N ~ 567 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 3 m/s^2 for 4 seconds. What is its final velocity?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a freely falling object near the Earth's surface, its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: In free fall neglecting air resistance, downward acceleration due to gravity is uniform and constant (g ~ 9.8 or 10 m/s^2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If a body starts from rest under uniform acceleration, the displacement covered is:
questions.explanation: From kinematic equation s = u*t + (1/2)*a*t^2, with u = 0, s = (1/2)*a*t^2, showing displacement is directly proportional to t^2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two cars A and B are moving along a straight road in the same direction at 54 km/h and 36 km/h respectively. What is the relative velocity of car A with respect to car B?
questions.explanation: v_rel = vA - vB = 54 km/h - 36 km/h = 18 km/h. Converting to SI units: 18 * (1000 m / 3600 s) = 5 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 5 m/s^2. How long will it take to reach a speed of 50 m/s?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the diagnostic purpose of an electroscope in electrostatics?
options: To identify whether a body is charged or neutral
To identify whether a body is an electrical conductor or insulator
To identify whether the sign of charge is positive or negative
All of the above can be tested using an electroscope
questions.explanation: A gold-leaf electroscope detects charge presence, classifies conductors vs insulators by charge leakage, and determines charge polarity via leaf divergence/convergence.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: How much tensile force is needed to stretch a 1 m wire of cross-sectional area 1 * 10^-6 m^2 by 1 mm if Young's modulus is 2 * 10^11 Pa?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The slope of a velocity versus time graph represents:
questions.explanation: Slope = Delta v / Delta t, which is the definition of acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A vehicle travelling at 20 m/s decelerates uniformly to complete rest in 5 seconds. What is its acceleration?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a body moving with uniform acceleration, its velocity-time graph is:
options: A straight line passing through the origin
A straight line with constant slope equal to acceleration
questions.explanation: Since acceleration is constant, the rate of change dv/dt is constant, yielding a linear graph with slope equal to a.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A car moving at 20 m/s applies brakes and comes to a stop in 10 seconds. What total distance does it cover before stopping?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following physical quantities is completely dimensionless?
questions.explanation: Strain is the ratio of change in length to original length (Delta L / L0), so its units cancel out completely.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A freely falling stone released from rest falls for 3 seconds. How far does it fall? (g = 10 m/s^2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body possesses a net negative charge of -6.4 nC. How many electrons are in excess? (Elementary charge e = 1.6 * 10^-19 C)
